title: Optimality of Assumption 1 for Tweakable Blockciphers
summary: The conjectured security level of a cascade of LRW2 constructions is treated as best possible for non-tweak-rekeyable tweakable blockciphers; whether that optimality assumption is reasonable remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Lampe and Seurin conjectured that a cascade of $\sigma$ LRW2 constructions achieves $2\sigma n/(\sigma+1)$ security, and Assumption 1 treats this level as the best possible for non-tweak-rekeyable tweakable blockciphers. The unresolved question is whether that optimality claim is reasonable.

scope.domain: Tweakable blockcipher security and the optimality of cascade constructions in the standard-versus-ideal model comparison.
parameters: σ: number of LRW2 constructions in the cascade
n: parameter in the conjectured security level
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether Assumption 1's claim that this level is best possible is reasonable.

citations.label: Insuperability of the Standard Versus Ideal Model Gap for Tweakable Blockcipher Security

progress.summary: The source presents the issue as the explicit question "Is Assumption 1 reasonable?", after recalling Lampe and Seurin's conjectured security level and Assumption 1's best-possible claim.
